title: Multi-sequence primer and deterministic warmup replayer
author: Priya Desai
description: Context: Long-tail latency spikes in steady-state runs were traced to nondeterministic warmup phases where sequence primer ordering and random trace replay caused noisy p95/p99 shifts. This PR introduces a deterministic warmup replayer plus a multi-sequence primer that lets workload runners reliably prime KV caches, prefix caches, and attention cache states for repeatable steady-state benchmarking. Motivation: Reduce noise in regression signals from warmup variance and make perf baselines reproducible across runs and CI shards. Goal is not to micro-optimize runtime, but to provide a reproducible priming path and a light-weight validation harness that guarantees same sequence ordering and timing semantics across hosts. Changes: - New bench/runner/deterministic_replayer.py: replay engine that accepts normalized traces and deterministic timing profiles. - New bench/runner/multi_sequence_primer.py: orchestrates interleaved sequences, supports prefix merging and synthetic token insertion for realistic priming. - bench/configs/deterministic_warmup.yaml: configuration presets (short/medium/long) used by CI and local profiling. - bench/utils/trace_normalizer.py: converts collected traces into canonical forms (canonical tokenization, anonymization of IDs, consistent timestamp deltas). - tests/integration/test_primer_replayer.py: integration coverage for determinism assertions across 3 seeds and 2 host types. - ci/workflows/bench.yml: adds a deterministic bench job that runs the warmup-only profile on PRs labeled "benchmark". Implementation notes: - Determinism is enforced by a combination of normalized traces and fixed rng seeds; we avoid global state where possible and expose a ReplayContext object to the runner. - The replayer can run in two modes: strict (asserts identical sequence of emitted tokens) and tolerant (allows whitespace/tokenizer variants but asserts same token ids after normalization). - The primer supports interleaving policy strategies (round-robin, weighted) to simulate multiplexed tenant scenarios. Performance impact: baseline warmup-only runs show p95 reduction variance from ±9.8% to ±2.1% over 20 repeated runs (local VM), and end-to-end benchmark CI runs show improved stability of baseline metrics (p95 confidence interval width reduced by ~3.6x). Checklist: - [x] Design doc walkthrough with ENG-7122 stakeholders - [x] Unit + integration tests - [x] CI job added and green - [x] Benchmarks added to baseline runbook - [x] Release notes drafted How to exercise locally: 1) python -m bench.runner.deterministic_replayer --config bench/configs/deterministic_warmup.yaml --trace samples/short_coldstart.trace 2) python -m bench.runner.multi_sequence_primer --mode strict --policy round-robin --runs 20 Notes and limitations: - This does not change serving runtime batching logic; it's purely a workload/priming harness. - Determinism guarantees apply only after trace normalization; traces collected from different tokenizer versions must be normalized first. - The replayer is intentionally lightweight; future work (ENG-7210) will add a golden-trace repository and artifact signing. Commits summary: see commits list for short descriptions. Merge: squash and merge to main after 2 approvals.
